content: The dose of brivaracetam should be increased by up to 100% (i.e., doubled) in patients receiving concurrent treatment with rifampin. Close monitoring is required because rifampin reduces the levels or effects of brivaracetam by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of bromocriptine by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of budesonide through the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Alternative therapies should be considered, as rifampin also affects CYP3A4 metabolism, further reducing budesonide's efficacy. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of buprenorphine (including buccal, subdermal implant, and transdermal forms) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is necessary, and therapy adjustments may be required. For patients on buprenorphine subdermal implants who require CYP3A4 inducers, monitor for withdrawal symptoms. If the CYP3A4 inducer cannot be discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should transition to a buprenorphine formulation that allows dose adjustments. If the CYP3A4 inducer is discontinued, monitor for signs of overmedication. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of bupropion by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of buspirone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels of butabarbital and butalbital by increasing their metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cabazitaxel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Rifampin increases the metabolism of cabotegravir, reducing its levels and effects. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure. Cabotegravir is metabolized by UGT1A1 and UGT1A9, and strong inducers of these enzymes should be avoided. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of cabozantinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If coadministration is necessary, increase the cabozantinib dose (40 mg/day for Cometriq or 20 mg/day for Cabometyx) and resume the previous dose 2–3 days after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inducer. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of caffeine by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of calcifediol and calcitriol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Drugs that stimulate microsomal hydroxylation reduce the half-life of calcifediol. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. Calcium carbonate decreases the absorption of rifampin. To avoid this interaction, administer rifampin at least one hour before antacids. Close monitoring is advised. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of canagliflozin by increasing its metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. For patients with an eGFR <73 mL/min/1.73 m², consider using an alternative antihyperglycemic agent. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. Cannabidiol also affects CYP2B6 metabolism, so dosage adjustments of CYP2B6 substrates may be necessary. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of capivasertib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of capmatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of carbamazepine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cariprazine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of carvedilol by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of caspofungin by increasing its metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Ceftobiprole medocaril sodium increases rifampin levels by inhibiting OATP1B1/1B3 transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of celecoxib by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cenobamate by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. Increase the dose of CYP2B6 substrates as needed. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of ceritinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cevimeline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of chloramphenicol by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of chlordiazepoxide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of chloroquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin increases the toxicity of cholic acid by reducing its elimination. Avoid inhibitors of the bile salt efflux pump (BSEP), as they may exacerbate the accumulation of conjugated bile salts in the liver, leading to clinical symptoms. If coadministration is necessary, monitor serum transaminases and bilirubin levels. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cilostazol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of cimetidine by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cinacalcet by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of citalopram by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Clofazimine reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of clomipramine by inducing CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of clonazepam by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin increases the metabolism of clopidogrel, potentially enhancing its antiplatelet effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug, and monitor for increased antiplatelet activity. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of clorazepate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Clotrimazole increases rifampin levels through an unspecified mechanism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Coadministration of rifampin with cotrimoxazole increases rifampin concentrations, potentially increasing the risk of toxicity. Monitor for adverse reactions during coadministration. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of clozapine by inducing CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the risk of therapeutic failure and resistance development. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of colchicine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of conivaptan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens (oral and vaginal forms) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of copanlisib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of cortisone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of crizotinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Crizotinib increases rifampin levels via P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of cyclophosphamide by inducing CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cyclosporine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of dabigatran by inducing P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dabrafenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin increases the levels of danicopan by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Caution is advised, and dose reductions of P-gp substrates may be necessary. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of dantrolene by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of daprodustat by inducing CYP2C8 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. Monitor hemoglobin levels and adjust daprodustat doses when initiating or discontinuing CYP2C8 inducers. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of dapsone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of daridorexant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of darifenacin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of darolutamide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration with combined P-gp and strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dasatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of daunorubicin by inducing P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of deferasirox by inducing UGT enzymes. Avoid coadministration with potent UGT inducers. If coadministration is necessary, consider increasing the initial deferasirox dose to 30 mg/kg and monitor ferritin levels and clinical response. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of deflazacort by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of deuruxolitinib by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C9 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of dexamethasone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of diazepam by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of diclofenac by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of digoxin by inducing P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of diltiazem by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of docetaxel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dolutegravir by inducing UGT1A and CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. Increase the dolutegravir dosage when coadministering with strong UGT1A/CYP3A4 inducers. Use an alternative to rifampin in patients with integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)-associated resistance substitutions or suspected INSTI resistance. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of donepezil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of doravirine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance development. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of doxepin cream by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of doxorubicin (including liposomal formulations) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of dronabinol by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dronedarone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of duloxetine by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dutasteride by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of duvelisib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inducing P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration with potent P-gp inducers.
